Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No documented integration of INEC electoral register with the NGDX data exchange platform. INEC has its own biometric voter register (BVAS) but cross-government data sharing with this system is not confirmed.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 relied only on the 2022 NITDA National Data Strategy PDF, which the cited URL returns a 403 error on and does not specifically address electoral data. Fresh search found reporting (Investors King, 4 Sept 2025) quoting INEC Chairman Mahmood Yakubu and NIMC Director-General Coker-Odusote confirming active INEC-NIMC collaboration toward a shared/single identity database, with NIMC officials being deployed to INEC registration centres to enable simultaneous NIN/voter registration. Corroborating reporting (Nairametrics, 20 Sept 2025) confirms the broader NGDX cross-government exchange itself is still pre-operational, with sector use cases due to roll out only from 2026. No source confirms operational integration, only stated intent/collaboration at planning stage. Value code revised from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Planned). Evidence rests on journalistic quotes of officials rather than a primary INEC/NITDA planning document, so flagged for human review before finalising.
revised_comments: INEC and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are collaborating to harmonise their biometric databases, with the aim of aligning the national voters' register with the NIMC identity database and enabling simultaneous National Identification Number and voter registration at Continuous Voter Registration centres. This data-sharing initiative sits at a planning and early-collaboration stage; it has not been formalised as an operational link to the Nigerian Data Exchange (NGDX), the government's forthcoming cross-agency data exchange platform, which itself remains in build-out with a phased sector rollout only beginning in 2026.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence of court records or justice system integration with Nigeria's data exchange infrastructure.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 relied only on the 2022 NITDA National Data Strategy PDF (URL returns 403 on refetch), with no specific finding either way on justice-sector integration. Fresh searches found active judiciary digitisation independent of the government data exchange: the Supreme Court launched a Nigerian Case Management System (NCMS) on 1 July 2026 covering e-filing and records for appeals (Tribune Online, Voice of Nigeria), and a vendor-marketed Criminal Justice Reporting Portal (LawPavilion/CJRP) claims integration across policing, courts and correctional agencies with NIMC ID linkage — this latter source is a vendor page and its actual deployment status could not be independently verified, so it is treated cautiously. Corroborating reporting (Nairametrics, 20 Sept 2025) confirms the NGDX cross-government exchange itself remains pre-operational, with sector use cases due to roll out only from 2026, and no source ties justice-sector records to NGDX specifically. Value code revised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated), reflecting confirmed current absence of cross-government integration rather than lack of information. Flagged for human review given interpretive judgement on whether judiciary-internal digitisation should affect this score and given the unverified vendor source.
revised_comments: Nigeria's judiciary is digitising case management independently of the national data exchange programme. The Supreme Court launched a Nigerian Case Management System in July 2026, covering electronic filing and records for appeals, with further phases planned, while a separate Criminal Justice Reporting Portal has been proposed to connect police, prosecutorial and correctional agencies with National Identification Number-linked records. However, the Nigerian Data Exchange (NGDX), the government's planned cross-agency data-sharing platform, remains in build-out, with sector use cases due to roll out only from 2026, and no public documentation links court or justice-sector records to it. Justice-sector data therefore remains outside the national data exchange for the time being.
